<thought>Based on the spectrum, the M+1 peak is ~16 % of the monoisotopic peak, consistent with many 13C atoms, indicating carbon is present. The M+2 peak is ~4–5 % of the base peak, matching the natural abundance of 34S, indicating sulfur is present. No 33 % M+2 pattern (chlorine) or 1:1 M/M+2 pattern (bromine) is observed, so those elements cannot be definitively identified. Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
